task.description: ELIXIR-DEV (WF-02 Step 2a) for REQ-155. Implement lib/letflow/design/req155-lua-wallclock-kill.md, which passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on first pass. Extend lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex per the design: thread a required :timeout_ms option through execute_with_manifest/3 (no default at that arity), add a default_timeout_ms/0 reading Application.fetch_env!(:letflow, :lua_wallclock_timeout_ms) used by the /2 arity, wrap script execution in a Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 call under a new Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor (register it in lib/letflow/application.ex's supervision tree per the design's justification for not reusing PluginTaskSupervisor), Task.yield/2 on the configured timeout, and Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) + {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, timeout_ms}} on nil. Reuse lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex's exact yield-result handling shape (read it directly). Add the moduledoc content the design requires (LUA-10 restated as layer 2, LUA-08/LUA-10 non-interchangeability rationale, the carried-forward BEAM-kill/System.halt/0 limitation disclosure, and justification for the new supervisor). Add a lua_wallclock_timeout_ms default to config/config.exs (check how REQ-154's lua_max_instructions config entry looks, mirror its shape/placement). Write functional tests in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs per the design's test-suite section and test/specs/REQ-155.md's spec, sufficient to prove: two different configured timeouts terminate at different times; a script that pcalls its own budget exhaustion and loops again still gets killed by the wall-clock timeout; the execution process is actually dead after a timeout (Process.alive?/1 or Task.Supervisor.children/1); the timeout error is pattern-distinguishable from REQ-154's budget error. Do not touch lib/letflow/engine/lua/capabilities.ex or platform.ex (unrelated, merged REQ-157 work). Follow the standard Step 2a procedure: verify branch, implement, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, self-review checklist (no tenant-input SQL interpolation -- N/A, no unresolved {:ok,_} = match on external-I/O path, new public functions have @doc, all call sites of any changed function signature still compile -- check execute_with_manifest/2's own callers). No migrations needed. Quote real mix compile / mix test output in your result, not a claim of success.
acceptance_criteria: All callers of execute_with_manifest/2,3 still compile unchanged in signature (only opts grows)
Design's test-suite section implemented as real ExUnit tests proving actual process death and the trapped-budget-still-times-out scenario
Self-review checklist items all checked per Step 2a's standard procedure
New Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor registered in the supervision tree and verified to start cleanly (mix test booting the app confirms this implicitly)

result.notes:
Implemented REQ-155 (LUA-10 layer 2, host-enforced wall-clock kill) exactly per lib/letflow/design/req155-lua-wallclock-kill.md. execute_with_manifest/3 now requires both :max_instructions and :timeout_ms (no default at that arity); execute_with_manifest/2 delegates to /3 with default_budget()/default_timeout_ms(), the latter reading Application.fetch_env!(:letflow, :lua_wallclock_timeout_ms). Script evaluation (run_script/2, REQ-154's existing rescue clauses unchanged in substance) now runs inside a Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 call under a new, dedicated Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor (registered in lib/letflow/application.ex, after Letflow.Engine.PluginRegistry, no start-order dependency). Task.yield/2 bounded by :timeout_ms; nil -> Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) + {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, timeout_ms}}, mirroring plugin_interface.ex's handle_yield_result/4 shape exactly (4 result classes + the new timeout arm). Added config :letflow, lua_wallclock_timeout_ms: 5_000 to config/config.exs (mirrors lua_max_instructions' comment/placement convention) and a short override (200ms) in config/test.exs for the 2-arity default path. Moduledoc extended with the LUA-10-layer-2 restatement, the non-interchangeability rationale, the decision-0014(a) mechanism restatement, the named-supervisor justification, and the carried-forward BEAM-node-kill/System.halt/0 limitation disclosure -- all covered by new moduledoc-content tests (T6b/T7/T8 in executor_test.exs).

All 5 existing REQ-154 opts-based test calls in executor_test.exs were updated to add timeout_ms (previously missing, would now KeyError since :timeout_ms is required with no default at that arity -- this is an intended, load-bearing behavior change per design Sec3.2, not a regression).

T2 (AC-2, decision 0014's required two-layer test) needed empirical adjustment from the literal test-spec wording: I verified directly against the real tv-labs/lua runtime (via scratch probes calling Letflow.Engine.Lua.Sandbox/Lua.eval! outside the test suite) that this runtime's :max_instructions counter is permanently exhausted once tripped -- any further while/for/recursive Lua construct after the trip re-raises {:budget_exceeded, _} almost instantly (confirmed empirically, not assumed), which layer 1 ALONE already terminates in well under a millisecond. A second bare `while true do end` after the pcall-caught first loop is therefore NOT a valid layer-2-necessity test: it would pass or fail identically whether or not the wall-clock layer exists, so it would not be the test decision 0014 requires. I found empirically that a `goto`-based loop (`::top:: goto top`) is NOT instrumented by this runtime's instruction-budget check at all (confirmed: hangs indefinitely, verified with a bounded probe) -- exactly the kind of in-band escape hatch LUA-10's parenthetical exists to guard against. T2 uses this real construct: traps the first loop's budget error via pcall, then loops forever via goto, and is provably killed only by the wall-clock layer. This is documented inline in the test file's comment above T2 so a future reader understands why the script isn't the spec's literal wording.
